key_insight: Universal YOCO (YOCO-U) fuses the YOCO decoder-decoder architecture with recursive computation to enable efficient test-time depth scaling, reducing loop overhead and KV-cache growth while preserving or improving reasoning performance.
problem_solved: Standard Transformer decoding strategies are inefficient for test-time scaling: repeated loops add compute overhead and the KV cache grows with model depth, limiting practical inference-time scaling of reasoning/agentic abilities.
method: Adopt YOCO decoder-decoder layout to structure decoding for depth-scalable inference.
Introduce recursive computation that reuses intermediate states instead of naive looping, sharply reducing per-step compute and KV cache footprint.
Coordinate model depth scaling and cache management so additional inference depth yields quality gains with sublinear compute/cache cost.
impact: YOCO-U makes test-time depth scaling practical and cost-effective, enabling LLMs to extend reasoning and agentic behavior at inference time with lower latency and memory overhead—valuable for deployment and research on scalable reasoning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: standard Transformer decoding (looping + growing KV cache) vs YOCO-U (decoder-decoder + recursive reuse).
Flowchart showing recursive computation reusing intermediate states across depth steps (arrowed loops with reduced memory icons).
Performance chart: quality (e.g., reasoning score) vs inference depth with compute/memory curves showing YOCO-U's efficiency advantage.
Icon panel: latency, memory, cost, and accuracy with callouts quantifying typical improvements (e.g., % latency or memory reduction).
paper_title: Universal YOCO for Efficient Depth Scaling
paper_authors: Yutao Sun, Li Dong, Tianzhu Ye, Shaohan Huang, Jianyong Wang
